title: AO/168/2011 of MOHAMMAD MIYA Vs ALI MOHAMMAD

paras.text:
HI GH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAI NI TAL
Ap p eal f r om Or d er No. 1 6 8 of 2 0 1 1
Mohamm ad Miya ... Appellant
Vs.
Ali Moham m ad and Others ... Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Mohd. Azim, Advocate, for the appellant.
 Mr. Basant Singh, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Harshpal
 Sekhon, Advocate, for the respondent Nos. 1 & 2.
 Mr. B.K. Gupta, Advocate, for respondent No. 3 through video
 conferencing.
Hon 'b le Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.
This Appeal from Order arises out of an award dated
05.05.2010, as it has been rendered by the learned Motor
Accident Claims Tribunal in MACC No. 392 of 2007, Ali
Mohd. and another Vs. Mohd. Miya and others.
2. This Appeal from Order stood admitted by the
coordinate Bench of this Court by an order dated
16.07.2013, but, owing to the fact that the parties to the
Appeal from Order have agreed to address the Appeal from
Order on merits, the same is being heard finally.
3. The claim ants respondent Nos. 1 & 2 herein had filed a
Claim Petition on 14.11.2007, praying for the grant of
com pensation to the tune of Rs. 25.00 lakh, on the ground
that in an accident which has chanced on 11.10.2007, due
to collision of the vehicles i.e. Motorcycle bearing
registration No. UA-06E-9453, along with other offending
vehicle i.e. HR-38H-1905, Mohd. Kabil Hussain had met with
the sad demise thus on account of which, they contended
that since they were the dependents on the deceased, they

2
were entitled to receive the com pensation as per the
provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
4. According to the Claim Petition, on the date of the
accident/ death, the deceased was 24 years of age and it
was contended by the claim ants that the deceased was
working as an electrician/ m echanic. Apart from that he was
also engaged in the business of agriculture and used to
respectively earned about Rs. 5,000/ - and Rs. 2,000/ - per
m onth. Thus, the total income, which was said to have
accrued to him i.e. deceased was Rs. 7,000/ - per m onth.
5. I t was further contended by the claim ants that his
engagement as an electrician was with the fabricators
workshop, which was being operated by one Mr. Rahees
Ahm ad. The matter was contested and the respective
parties filed their respective statements. The written
statement thus filed by the owner of the Truck was
num bered as Paper no. 15(kha) along with its driver the
opposite party No. 2 to the claim petition.
6. I n the written statement thus filed by the present
appellant on 21.04.2008, what is im portant is that none of
the pleadings has been raised by the appellant herein before
the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, to get a finding
returned with regard to the plea of contributory negligence,
as argued by the learned counsel for the appellant, which
are apparently contrary to the pleadings of the written
statement and even contrary to the issue fram ed by the
learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal and even contrary to
the grounds which had been taken in the present Appeal
from Order, to the effect that they would not be liable to

3
pay any com pensation because the accident, as alleged it
was an act of "contributory negligence" because there was a
head on collusion due to which the death has taken place of
late Mr. Mohd. Kabil Hussain.
7. The I nsurance Com pany contested the proceedings by
filing a separate written statem ent and in the written
statement thus filed by them , they have come up with the
case that they would not be liable to pay any com pensation
as such to the claim ants for the reason being that on the
date of accident the offending vehicle i.e. the Truck bearing
registration No. HR-38H-1905 was being rashly and
negligently driven by the driver of the offending vehicle and
further that they would not be liable to pay any
com pensation to the claim ants, because of the fact that the
vehicle since was being driven contrary to the term s of the
policy, thus in the light of the provisions contained under
sub Section (6) of Section 158 of the Act, the I nsurance
Company would not be liable to pay any am ount of
com pensation to the claim ants, qua the claim raised
therein, coupled with the fact, that the vehicle was being
driven by the driver of the vehicle in contravention to the
provisions contained under Section 64(V-B) of the I nsurance
Act.
8. A specific plea was taken by the Insurance Company by
filing a written statement on 03.10.2008, that the entire
proceedings of the claim petition raised by the respondent
Nos. 1 & 2 would be vitiated for the reason being the other
vehicle, which was said to be involved in the motorcycle
accident; in order to develop and establish the plea of
contributory negligence, since was not m ade as a party nor

4
the I nsurance Com pany of the m otorcycle which was also
said to be involved in the accident was m ade a party thus it
was contended that the claim petition would be deserved to
be rejected on that ground.
9. Despite the fact that after the exchange of pleading the
I nsurance Com pany had brought the facts on record with
regard to the violation of the term s of the policy and the
m anner in which the vehicle was being driven by the driver
who was employed by the present appellant, coupled with
the plea taken by the insurance com pany to the effect that
the proceedings under Section 166 to be read with Section
140 of the Motor Vehicle Act would be bad due to non-joinder of the necessary party. No effort was ever m ade by
the present appellant or even the claim ants, ought to m ove
application, as such, before the learned Motor Accident
Claim s Tribunal, praying for to implead the owner of the
m otorcycle as well as its insurance com pany, in order to
develop and prove his plea pertaining to the act of
contributory negligence as argued now at the stage of
appeal.
10. The argument as it has been extended by the learned
counsel for the appellant, for the first time, in this Appeal
from Order with regard to the com pensation which has been
leveled against them, that the sam e would be bad because
it was an accident which has chanced on 11.10.2007, due to
the act of contributory negligence, because it was a head on
collusion, the said aspect could have only been proved and
established by evidence when the owner and the insurance
com pany of the other offending vehicle i.e. m otorcycle
which was involved in the accident and also was m ade as a

5
party to the proceedings because the factum of contributory
negligence cannot be isolatedly decided by impleadm ent of
one of the offending vehicle, which was involved in the
accident i.e. the truck owned by the appellant herein.
Because that aspect could had been decided only when the
owner and the insurance com pany were got m ade as a
party before Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal, it would have
been then only this aspect could have decided, and could
have been considered by his Court even at the appellate
stage.
11. The defence of contributory negligence was a defence
which has been raised by the appellant. Hence they were
m ore im portantly required to shoulder their responsibility to
have m oved an appropriate application for raising the plea
about the effect of non-joinder of the necessary party or
particularly by raising a plea with regard to the contributory
negligence and accordingly getting the issues form ulated
before the learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal, that the
proceedings of Case No. 392 of 2007 would be vitiated due
to non joinder of necessary party and no liability of paym ent
of com pensation could be harnessed upon the appellant,
because of the fact that since it was a case of contributory
negligence, they ought to have got an issue form ulated
before the learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal, which
was not done, hence, they would be estopped from raising a
question of contributory negligence, now for the first tim e
before the Appellate Court and that too without there being
any specific ground taken in the Mem orandum of Appeal as
preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

6
12. The I nsurance Com pany in the written statement have
com e up with plea that since the vehicle, which was insured
with the insurance com pany i.e. respondent No. 3 herein,
they have contended that apart from the fact that the
vehicle was being driven contrary to the provisions of the
insurance cover; apart from that it has been argued by the
learned counsel for the respondent No. 3, that even the
documentary evidence which was placed on record by the
appellant himself herein in relation to the driver who was
driving the offending vehicle at the relevant point of tim e
when the accident has chanced, the exhibit which was
m arked as paper No. 18C/ 8, which was the driving license
of the offending truck, was issued by Assistant Regional
Transport Officer, Ram pur, UP, which was by way of a Form
No. 6, issued under Rule 6(1), wherein it was specifically
observed by the com petent licensing authority, that the
driver of the vehicle was holding the license to drive "light
m otor vehicle" and not for "heavy goods vehicle".
13. Since the appellant himself has placed the said
document on record to be read in evidence by the learned
Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal, they cannot now take a
som ersaulted plea, a stand that on the date of the accident,
the driver Habib Ahm ed who was engaged by them to drive
the vehicle, was having a valid license to drive the vehicle.
14. The aforesaid contention further stands denounced
because during the pendency of this Appeal from Order, the
appellant have filed an Application under Order 41 Rule 27,
allegedly bringing on record the driving license which they
contended that it was being held by the driver on the date
of accident in order to show that he was validly driving the

7
vehicle which was of a heavy goods vehicle but since the
Application under Order 41 Rule 22, was lastly dismissed by
the coordinate Bench of this Court on 30.06.2023, the same
cannot now be taken into consideration for the purposes of
establishm ent of his argument that the driver at the time of
the accident was having a valid license as it has been
argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No. 3,
that no liability could be fastened upon them because the
driver engaged by the appellant was not having a valid
driving license hence the entire liability was to be fastened
upon the owner of the vehicle and not to the insurance
com pany.
15. Based on the aforesaid pleading, the learned Motor
Accident Claim s Tribunal has fram ed the following issues,
which are extracted hereunder: -

16. The respective parties lead their evidence in relation to
their respective cases for their defence and for the claim
before the learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal and the
driving license which was placed on record was also a
subject m atter which was considered by the learned Motor

8
Accident Claim s Tribunal while deciding issue No. 2, about
its validity and its impact upon fixation of liability on the
insurance company.
17. As far as the quantification of com pensation is
concerned, that is not an aspect which has been argued by
the learned counsel for the appellant before this Court,
accepting it as determined by the learned Motor Accident
Claim s Tribunal, while deciding issue No. 4 as to what would
be the appropriate compensation which could be determined
to be m ade payable to the claim ants on account of the
death of Mr. Mohd. Kabil Hussain based on the income
proved to be accruing to him .
18. Since no question has been raised, qua the
quantification of the compensation and particularly in the
context of the incom e accruing to the deceased, the learned
Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal has rightly determ ined the
m onthly income of the deceased as to be Rs. 7,000/ - per
m onth, and determining it by a m ultiplier of 12 as to be Rs.
36,000/ - per annum incom e which accrued to the deceased
and after m aking deductions, the am ount of Rs. 18,000/ -
was taken as to be the dependency for the claim ants based
on which and after applying the m ultiplier of 18 taking into
consideration the age of the deceased on the date of the
accident, the am ount of compensation which has been
determined as to be Rs. 3,36,000/ - has been rightly
determined by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
which calls for no interference by this Court.
19. I t is a settled law that if a party to a proceedings raises
a defence, it's always the burden which has to be

9
discharged by him to establish, that the liability could not
have been fastened upon him being the owner of the vehicle
and the driver engaged by him was driving the vehicle
contrary to the provisions of the I nsurance Act, as well as
about the validity of the insurance policy of the vehicle
which was utterly failed to be discharged by the appellant
before the learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal. Thus,
the im pugned award as rendered on 05.05.2010 does not
suffer from any apparent error or it is not in violation to the
argument of the learned counsel for the appellant before
this Court as observed above. Thus, the Appeal from Order
lacks m erit; the sam e is dismissed.
20. The amount, as deposited by the appellant in
pursuance to the interim order passed by this Court and the
part of it, which has been disbursed to the claim ants, the
balance amount would be paid to the claim ants by the
learned Motor Accident Claim s Tribunal in accordance with
law along with the interest which has accrued on the same,
after deducting the am ount which has been permitted to be
withdrawn by the orders passed by this Court. Let the
statutory am ount be remitted back to the learned Motor
Accident Claim s Tribunal, for its appropriate adjustm ent and
disbursement as directed above.
21. Subject to the aforesaid, the Appeal from Order stands
dismissed.
( Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.)
